description:
A HIP event wrapper in the kernels crate's device host layer, returning the elapsed device time of a kernel span so a measurement can separate kernel execution from allocation, copy, and host serialization.

## Background

Every GPU figure recorded for the permanent kernels so far is a wall-clock span around a whole dispatch: host serialization of the batch, two device allocations, a host-to-device copy, the launch, a device synchronize, a device-to-host copy, and two frees. Kernel-only duration cannot be recovered from it, and no HIP event is used anywhere in `crates/gf2-kernels-hip` today.

Event objects are device resources acquired and released through the HIP FFI, which is the same category as the buffers, streams, and launch dimensions the crate already owns. `crates/gf2-kernels-hip/src/host/` exports `DeviceBuffer`, `PinnedHostBuffer`, `HipStream`, `HipStreamPool`, and `LaunchDims`; events belong beside them. The crate reaches the HIP runtime through one raw-ABI path — thin `extern "C"` shims in `hip/host_runtime.hip` with their Rust declarations in `src/ffi.rs`, the way the stream and allocation infrastructure is bound today — and the event entry points enter through that same path rather than through a second binding mechanism. A private event helper inside a research crate would duplicate a shared device-resource mechanism, which the repository's convention-convergence rule treats as a defect unless it is a named exception.

One event pair is also not enough on its own. A dispatch is four distinct spans — the host-to-device copy, the kernel, the device-to-host copy, and the launch interval around the submission — and a study that reports transfer cost separately from kernel cost needs all four from a single run rather than from repeated runs with pieces removed. The API therefore records a phase-tagged sequence of event spans across one dispatch.

Launch overhead needs one more rule, because the obvious definition is unsound: the interval between a host-side enqueue timestamp and the kernel start event subtracts a host timestamp from a device timestamp, and a difference across two clocks is not a duration. The boundary instead reports two quantities, each on its own clock — the host-side duration of the submission call itself, and the device-only elapsed time from a marker event recorded on the launch stream at submission to the kernel start event — and never combines them arithmetically.

An event pair alone also does not isolate kernel time here. The permanent dispatchers launch on the default stream and call a device-wide synchronize inside the dispatch, so a caller bracketing that call measures the synchronize rather than the kernel. Isolating the kernel needs a launch boundary that records the start and stop events on the launch stream around the kernel itself and returns without a device-wide sync, leaving the caller to await the stop event. That boundary is part of this work.

The boundary also cannot be built on the kernel entry points as they stand: every permanent kernel entry point hard-codes the default stream — `hipLaunchKernelGGL(…, /*stream=*/0, …)` in each of the three `hip/permanent/permanent_bipedal*.hip` sources — so no caller-supplied stream can reach a permanent kernel today. Stream-bearing variants of the batch launch entry points, taking a `hipStream_t` through the FFI, are part of this work; the existing entry points keep their behaviour by delegating to the variants on the default stream.

The existing dispatch entry points keep their current synchronous contract: production callers are unaffected, and the instrumented boundary is an additional surface rather than a change to the shipped one.

This is production `unsafe` in the crate that is permitted to hold it, so each FFI boundary carries its own safety contract.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `crates/gf2-kernels-hip/src/host/` exposes an event type that acquires a HIP event on construction and releases it on drop, with no path that leaks the event on an error return.
- [hard] REQ-02: The event entry points — create, destroy, record, query, and elapsed time — are bound through the crate's existing raw-ABI path, as `extern "C"` shims in `hip/host_runtime.hip` with declarations in `src/ffi.rs`, each declaration carrying its safety contract, with no second binding mechanism introduced.
- [hard] REQ-03: The API records a start event and a stop event on a caller-supplied stream and returns the elapsed device time between them in milliseconds.
- [hard] REQ-04: Querying elapsed time before the stop event has completed returns a stated error rather than a partially observed duration.
- [hard] REQ-05: Every `unsafe` block the change introduces carries an explicit safety contract naming the precondition it relies on.
- [hard] REQ-06: An event-instrumented launch boundary records the start and stop events on the launch stream around the kernel and returns without calling a device-wide synchronize, so the reported duration covers the kernel rather than the enclosing dispatch.
- [hard] REQ-07: The instrumented boundary lets the caller supply the stream it launches on, and reports the elapsed kernel time once the stop event has completed.
- [hard] REQ-08: Each permanent batch launch entry point has a stream-bearing variant that accepts a caller-supplied `hipStream_t` and launches the kernel on that stream, and the existing entry points launch on the default stream by delegating to the variants, so their behaviour is unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-09: The boundary records a phase-tagged sequence of event spans across one dispatch and returns the host-to-device copy duration, the kernel duration, and the device-to-host copy duration separately, so a caller attributes time to a phase without a second run.
- [hard] REQ-10: The boundary reports launch overhead as two separately reported quantities — the host-side duration of the submission call, and the device-only elapsed time between a marker event recorded on the launch stream at submission and the kernel start event — and no reported figure subtracts a host timestamp from a device timestamp.
- [hard] REQ-11: A phase the caller did not perform is reported as absent rather than as a zero duration.
- [hard] REQ-12: The existing permanent dispatch entry points keep their current synchronous behaviour and signatures, so a production caller observes no change.
- [hard] REQ-13: A device-gated test records a span around a known-duration kernel and asserts the returned duration is positive and strictly smaller than the wall-clock span of the enclosing synchronous dispatch of the same work.
- [hard] REQ-14: A device-gated test over a dispatch with both copies asserts that the three phase durations are each positive and that their sum does not exceed the enclosing wall-clock span.
- [hard] REQ-15: Device-touching tests are gated on the crate's `hip` feature and marked ignored with a reason naming the required device, matching the convention of the crate's existing test files.
- [hard] REQ-16: `cargo test --manifest-path crates/gf2-kernels-hip/Cargo.toml --release --features hip` compiles on a ROCm host, with the device-gated tests reported as ignored when no device is present.

## Notes

`crates/gf2-kernels-hip` is excluded from the default Cargo workspace and requires ROCm, so the workspace CI pipeline never compiles it; the explicit `--manifest-path` invocation above is the only build evidence for this change.

Scope is the event API, the stream-bearing launch variants, the instrumented launch boundary, and their tests. No measurement, receipt, or harness wiring belongs here.
title: HIP event timing API for device-side kernel spans
